title: More Numerically Accurate Algorithm for Stiff Matrix Exponential

affiliations.1: Department of Mathematics, Ariel University, Ariel 4070000, Israel; svetlanabu@ariel.ac.il
affiliations.2: Department of Cancer Biology, Cancer Institute, University College London, London WC1E 6BT, UK

abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel, highly accurate numerical algorithm for matrix exponentials (MEs). The algorithm is based on approximating Putzer’s algorithm by analytically solving the ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based coefficients and approximating them. We show that the algorithm outperforms other ME algorithms for stiff matrices for several matrix sizes while keeping the computation and memory consumption asymptotically similar to these algorithms. In addition, we propose a numerical-error- and complexity-optimized decision tree model for efficient ME computation based on machine learning and genetic programming methods. We show that, while there is not one ME algorithm that outperforms the others, one can find a good algorithm for any given matrix according to its properties.
keywords: decision tree for a numerical algorithm
summary: We propose a new, highly accurate numerical algorithm for computing matrix exponentials, built by approximating Putzer's algorithm through analytically solving and approximating its coefficients. It outperforms other matrix exponential algorithms for stiff matrices of several sizes while keeping computation and memory costs asymptotically similar. We also built a decision tree model, using machine learning and genetic programming, that picks a good algorithm for a given matrix based on its properties, since no single algorithm is best for all.
key_findings: The new algorithm outperforms other matrix exponential algorithms for stiff matrices across several matrix sizes.
Its computation and memory consumption remain asymptotically similar to those of existing algorithms.
A decision tree model optimized for numerical error and complexity selects an efficient algorithm for each matrix.
No single matrix exponential algorithm outperforms the others, but a good one can be found for any matrix from its properties.
